experiment: SG052 fixed trailing100 HAC3 z=4.327111573414373 at checkpoint prefixes of length 100,140,180,220,240. For each n<240 alter only suffix with increasing ramp, decreasing ramp and deterministic permutation. Recompute classification from same acquired prefix. At each checkpoint serialize/deserialize original prefix, append canonical SHA256 event and verify independent hash-chain replay. Negative-control classifier intentionally reads final suffix. Compare checkpoint prediction to programmed final post-change direction separately.

pilot.disclosure: Pilot executed before freeze, includes prefreeze correction to exclude vacuous final-checkpoint suffix edits.

findings: No tested prefix decision changed when unseen suffix was altered across 12,960 challenges; JSON prefix replay and chained event verification passed.
Deliberately leaky negative control changed 7,902 times, demonstrating meaningful attack power of perturbations.
Observed full240 accuracy still limited: 433 correct, 42 wrong, 605 unresolved. Causal validity does not establish decision quality.
Earlier checkpoints should not be mistaken for committed decisions: at 100 observations 332 are wrong relative to final target.
The SHA256 event chain can identify history modifications only if its reference root is retained; this audit does not establish tamper-resistant external storage.
limitations: Causal noninterference tests cover these three specified mutation operators and checkpoints, not all possible dependencies.
Test uses same synthetic generator family as SG052 with new seeds, not externally heldout real-world data.
Negative-control sensitivity 7902/12960 is conditional on tested perturbations, not a false-positive rate.
Every prefix produces a diagnostic label; no early-stop commit gate was introduced or evaluated.
GitHub script imports the SG052 sibling, locally equivalent earlier source was executed; clean checkout runtime has not been independently verified.
